item.title: FG disagrees with W/Bank over H1 124% debt servicing/revenue ratio
item.description: Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has disagreed with the World Bank on the latter’s debt servicing/revenue ratio for the first half of 2026, put at 124 percent. The bank in its recent Nigeria Development Update (NDU) reported that federal government debt servicing was 124 percent above its revenue. However, the Federal Ministry of Finance, in a statement, yesterday, faulted the bank’s analysis, explaining that the debt servicing figure included those of the state governments and that it was, therefore, wrong to analyse it against the federal government revenue for the period under consideration. The statement read in part, “This conclusion is misleading, for three reasons, the government said. “The interest figure includes debt the Federal Government services on behalf of other tiers of government, including external loans to states. “Measuring this against federal revenue alone overstates the ratio which is only meaningful when debt and revenue cover the same level of government. “The reported revenue is also incomplete. It excludes independent revenue already earned by government agencies and enterprises but not yet remitted to the Treasury. ” In addition, more revenue is typically earned in the second half of the year than in the first due to the statutory timing of certain tax payments. This is why the ratio stood at 156% in H1 2025, while the full-year 2025 debt-service-to-revenue ratio was below 60%, down from 97% before the reforms. ” This is a clear sign of the progress delivered by the current administration’s reforms. “Between the first half of 2025 and the first half of 2026, federal revenue rose by 72%, from ₦3.6 trillion to ₦6.2 trillion. Atiku said the plight of serving and retired officers demanded urgent action on police welfare, including a salary review and resolution of the pension concerns raised by retirees, following the pay increase approved for members of the Armed Forces. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, on October 18, Atiku recounted cases of retired officers allegedly living on inadequate pensions, searching for menial jobs and begging for alms after decades of service. “Men and women who answered Nigeria’s call for decades are now waiting outside its legislature for Nigeria to answer theirs. Bola Tinubu should be ashamed that it has come to this,” he said. item.title: Barca defenders Garcia, Kounde doubt for PSG, Real Madrid clash
item.description: Barcelona defenders Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde have sustained injuries ahead of important matches against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League and Real Madrid in La Liga, the Spanish champions said Sunday. Spanish centre-back Garcia will miss both games and spend between “three to four weeks” out with a thigh injury, Barca said in a statement. Right-back Kounde suffered an ankle sprain and Barca said he would miss the trip to face PSG on Tuesday but may still be able to feature in the Clasico on Sunday, October 25, depending on the “evolution of the injury”. Both defenders ended the club’s 5-2 win over Real Betis in La Liga on Saturday with discomfort. Hansi Flick’s side won a ninth consecutive league game to continue their 100 percent start to the campaign. Double-defending European champions PSG announced a defensive absence of their own after Portuguese left-back Nuno Mendes picked up a knock in Saturday’s Ligue 1 win at Strasbourg. “Having sustained an injury to his left thigh during last night’s match against RC Strasbourg Alsace, Nuno Mendes will be sidelined for the next few weeks,” PSG posted on their website. item.title: ADC Campaign to Kwankwaso: Declare for APC if you share its agenda
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has challenged Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso to openly declare for the All Progressives Congress (APC) if he shares its political agenda, accusing him of attacking opposition figures while sparing President Bola Tinubu’s administration. The Council said Kwankwaso, the vice-presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), whose presidential candidate is Peter Obi, should be holding the ruling party accountable for the country’s worsening economic hardship and insecurity rather than repeatedly targeting ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar. In a statement on Sunday, ADC-PCC Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, dismissed Kwankwaso’s response to the Council’s earlier criticism as diversionary, insisting that it failed to address concerns over his political priorities. “Why is Senator Kwankwaso making our candidate the issue instead of confronting the ruling APC, whose policies have made life increasingly difficult for millions of Nigerians?” the Council asked. It listed hunger, insecurity, high fuel prices, the depreciation of the naira and mounting economic hardship among the issues it said should command the attention of opposition politicians. The Council questioned why Kwankwaso’s attacks appeared more frequently directed at Atiku and the ADC than at the APC government over the country’s challenges. “For the avoidance of doubt, the ADC cannot and will not be distracted by Senator Kwankwaso,” it declared. Describing the ADC as an increasingly accepted political platform, the Council said it remained focused on mobilising Nigerians around its promise to rescue the country from what it called the failures of APC governance. It also accused Kwankwaso of seeking political favour from the ruling party through his attacks on the ADC, urging him to demonstrate his political position openly rather than continue targeting the opposition party. The ADC-PCC reaffirmed its commitment to presenting Nigerians with an alternative in the 2027 general election, ending its response with a direct challenge to Kwankwaso: align openly with the APC if he shares its agenda. Shettima spoke at the weekend during the inauguration of the Bauchi Shettima Forum for Asiwaju (BASFA) in Bauchi. He was represented at the event by the Minister of State for Regional Development, Uba Maigari Ahmadu. The vice-president said several projects were being implemented through the North-East Development Commission (NEDC) to address the region’s developmental challenges, adding that more projects would be inaugurated in Bauchi and other North-East states in the coming months. He cited the ongoing construction of the Akwanga-Jos-Bauchi-Borno road as a major federal infrastructure project expected to improve connectivity and stimulate economic activities. According to him, the road is being constructed with reinforced concrete to ensure durability. “Work is currently ongoing on this project, utilising modern construction techniques. It is a high-quality road being built with reinforced concrete. We are actively working on it, and I can assure you that construction will reach Bauchi town very soon,” he said. Shettima attributed the administration’s regional development initiatives to the establishment of the Ministry of Regional Development and five regional development commissions to address the peculiar needs of different parts of the country. He urged Bauchi residents to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, saying the ongoing interventions demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to the region’s development. item.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu in Israel’s upcoming election
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Sunday offered his “complete and total” endorsement of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the country’s October 27 elections. “Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel. BIBI NETANYAHU WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN!,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister who is in a tight race to win a new mandate, quickly acknowledged Trump’s gesture. “Thank you, President Trump, for your tremendous support and for our work together. Together we will complete the mission!” Netanyahu wrote on X. In his post, Trump described Netanyahu as “a Great Warrior Prime Minister” and ally in the war against Iran that began in late February with a massive bombing campaign but has dragged on as Tehran has retaliated by blocking global energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz. Trump asserted that without Netanyahu as Israel’s leader, the United States would be alone in combating the threat from the Islamic regime, “with its 51 year old chant, ‘Death to Israel, Death to America! We will destroy the Little Satan and the Big Satan.'” “If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” the US president said. “This is the kind of Partner that the United States of America is demanding of Israel, a Country for which it has done so much,” he added. msp/md The post Trump endorses Netanyahu in Israel’s upcoming election appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Buhari saw Tinubu as ‘Bad News’ for Nigeria — Baba-Ahmed
item.description: — PRP chairman says ex-president resisted pressure to back Tinubu in 2023 Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, national chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), has claimed that former President Muhammadu Buhari was reluctant to transfer power to President Bola Tinubu in 2023 because he considered him “bad news” for Nigeria. Baba-Ahmed spoke at a summit organised by the Northern Elders Forum, in a video published on Symfoni’s YouTube channel on Saturday. He said Nigerians should have questioned Tinubu’s presidential ambition when he declared “Emilokan”, meaning “it is my turn”, during the build-up to the 2023 general election. “Nigerians ought to have known there was something wrong the day Tinubu said, ‘It’s my turn’. Maybe we missed it,” he said. “We have a presidency of a country of 250 million people. My turn? To do what? To become president.” Baba-Ahmed said Buhari was reluctant to hand over power to Tinubu after considering the implications of his presidency for the country. “Even Buhari saw Tinubu as bad news for this country. In fairness to him, he is not around him. Buhari resisted some people who insisted it had to be Tinubu,” he said. The PRP chairman criticised Tinubu’s administration, alleging that the country had deteriorated under his leadership. “Now we are being depressed for having a president for three and a half years. He has dragged the country as low as it is possible to go. And it has to stop him. We cannot go below, beyond where we are,” Baba-Ahmed said. He, however, expressed confidence in Nigerians’ ability to overcome the country’s challenges, saying the nation had survived major crises in the past. “We are very resilient people. item.title: Speaker Abbas mobilises grassroots support for Tinubu, APC candidates in Kaduna
item.description: Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, has urged Kaduna citizens to re-elect President Bola Tinubu and all APC candidates to sustain ongoing reforms and development projects in the state. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that Abbas made the call on Sunday in continuation of the tour of his constituency to inaugurate projects. Speaking during a groundbreaking ceremony for road construction and educational projects in Ikara Local Government Area, Abbas said the sacrifices associated with the Federal Government’s reforms were temporary. He expressed optimism that Nigerians would soon begin to experience the benefits. He urged Nigerians to give Tinubu a second term to complete the reforms, calling him a friend of Kaduna State. The Speaker said Kaduna benefited from four federal university projects within three years under Tinubu’s administration, after decades without another federal university. He listed the upgrade of the Federal College of Education, Zaria, to a university, the establishment of the University of Applied Sciences in Kachia and the conversion of the Kaduna petroleum institute into a university. Abbas also said a bill he sponsored secured presidential approval to convert Kaduna Polytechnic into a Federal University of Technology. He said the development, along with other federal projects, justified Kaduna residents supporting Tinubu’s re-election bid. Abbas also urged residents to support Gov. Uba Sani’s re-election in 2027, citing ongoing road, water and health projects across the state. He warned that a change of government could jeopardise the completion of ongoing projects, urging citizens to support continuity. The Speaker commended Uba Sani for his contributions to Kaduna State’s development and support for his emergence as Speaker of the House of Representatives. He also solicited support for the APC candidates in Kaduna, thanking the party for its support and contributions to development in the state. In his remarks, Gov. Uba Sani, represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Dr AbdulKadir Meyere, commended the Speaker for extending development projects to communities across the state. Gov. Sani also solicited support for all APC candidates in the state for continuity and to sustain the dividends of democracy. item.title: ‘France Is Burning,’ ‘Shattered’ By Immigration, Says Trump
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Sunday blamed immigration for unrest during protests in France and urged the country to tighten its migration rules. “France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country,” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform. “Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!” France was reeling Sunday from widespread damage during protests the day before that, which left a historic town hall torched and led to 1,800 arrests, piling pressure on President Emmanuel Macron six months before elections to replace him. This photograph shows a portion of the partially burnt facade of the Limoges city hall a day after riot and looting following nationwide protests against the “high cost of living” in Limoges on October 18, 2026. PASCAL LACHENAUD / AFP Trump’s post follows similar comments from Vice President JD Vance on Saturday. “Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion. They ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility. They were told it would lead to this, and they didn’t listen,” Vance wrote on X. “I pray that France, a beautiful country of amazing people, will stop this madness before more of its landmarks burn,” he added. Vance, seen as a potential presidential candidate in the 2028 election, also linked it to upcoming midterm races for congressional seats on November 3, where Republicans are not expected to perform well. item.description: Discussions on financing the planned extension of the Lagos Mass Transit Red Line to Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA) are at an advanced stage, the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Olubunmi Onabanjo-Kuku, has said. The project, planned by the Federal Government in collaboration with FAAN, will link the airport’s three terminals to the Red Line as part of the wider MMIA modernisation project. Speaking as a keynote panellist at the World Aviation Festival in Lisbon, Portugal, Kuku said efforts were ongoing to finalise the project’s financing structure. “We are actually working on completing the financing of the capital structure for that project,” she said. Kuku explained that the rail link would improve access between the city and the airport, with five stops within the airport serving its terminals and cargo facilities. “It allows us to connect the city very quickly to the airport with five stops within our airport. It connects our terminals and links our cargo terminals to the last stop,” she said, adding that the project would involve collaboration between the Lagos State and Federal Governments. FAAN MD Olubunmi Onabanjo-Kuku speaking as a keynote panellist at the World Aviation Festival in Lisbon, Portugal. On the ongoing upgrade of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Kuku said the project would make the facility more efficient and passenger-friendly through improved infrastructure and modern technology. Business and broadcasting implications: Broadband expansion could improve streaming quality, OTT distribution, mobile news consumption and access to digital services outside major cities. It also creates potential opportunities for telecommunications operators, fibre-network developers, digital publishers and infrastructure investors. What to watch: Investor commitments, project financing, broadband deployment contracts and the proportion of announced financing that becomes operational investment. 3. NIGERIA 2027: ARMY CHIEF VISITS BORNO AS ELECTION-SECURITY PREPARATIONS INTENSIFY The Chief of Army Staff Waidi Shaibu posing with officers and soldiers during the graduation of some soldiers from Exercise RESTORE HOPE X. X/@HQNigerianArmy What happened: Chief of Army Staff Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu visited Maiduguri on Saturday, 17 October, following President Tinubu’s directive to security agencies to intensify operations against terrorists and kidnappers. The army chief visited the headquarters of Operation Hadin Kai, the military’s principal counterinsurgency operation in the North-East. The presidential directive, announced after Thursday’s National Security Council meeting, also requires security agencies to provide a safe environment for the January 2027 general elections. The visit is confirmed, although no operational breakthrough or new rescue outcome has been independently established as a consequence. Why it matters: Insecurity remains a practical obstacle to electoral participation, particularly in communities affected by insurgency, displacement and kidnapping. Nigeria’s presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for 16 January 2027, followed by governorship and state assembly elections on 6 February. item.title: EU To Offer €20m Defence Support For Nigerian Armed Forces
item.description: The European Union (EU) is planning to provide €20 million in defence assistance to the Armed Forces of Nigeria (AFN) under the European Peace Facility. The proposed support was discussed when the Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, met with the EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, at Ship House in Abuja. In a statement on Saturday, the minister’s Special Assistant on Media, Leah Katung-Babatunde, said an EU technical delegation would visit Abuja in November to agree on the details of the assistance. The meeting also reviewed security cooperation between Nigeria and the EU, with Mignot commending Musa’s efforts to improve the country’s security situation. The ambassador also invited the minister to a meeting of defence ministers in Brussels later this year. The Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, met with the EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, at Ship House in Abuja. Musa thanked the EU for its continued support and reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to protecting lives and promoting national development. He said relative peace was gradually returning to troubled parts of the country through the efforts of the armed forces and other security agencies, although kidnapping along major highways and attacks on isolated communities remained a challenge. The minister also disclosed that Nigeria was expecting the delivery of 10 attack helicopters, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and other military equipment to strengthen security operations. On regional security, Musa identified the shrinking of the Lake Chad Basin, which supports more than 50 million people, as a potential source of instability. He said denying terrorists access to holding areas on the Lake Chad islands remained a key operational priority for the Multinational Joint Task Force. On the Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration (DDR) programme, the minister stressed that the initiative should prioritise victims of the conflict, including affected military personnel. Mignot also commended a recent conference of past and present MNJTF force commanders, attended by representatives of the African Union and the Lake Chad Basin Commission.
